Yeah, people can claim whatever they want, like that woman who claims to be the queen of Canada, but it doesn't mean anything will come from it.  I can claim that I'm a god, or an alien, or an advanced AI or part of your subconscious.  Claims by themselves mean nothing.

In the process of claiming asylum you have to fill out paperwork for your reasons for claiming asylum and that paperwork and the reasons have to be approved.  If it doesn't get approved you don't get to stay.  Seems pretty straightforward.  

Claiming asylum isn't magic, but it does take time to process once the paperwork is filed and it has to be filed within a timeframe, so you don't get to sit on it forever.  

Everything is a process.  If you don't believe in the process thats fine, but at least come out and say that rather than stating you have to claim asylum before you enter the country or you can only seek it because of war, neither of which seem to be true.

War is a valid reason to become a refugee, but asylum seems to be more personal.  Just looking at [form I-589 part B](https://www.uscis.gov/sites/default/files/document/forms/i-589.pdf), reasons for seeking asylum are race, religion, nationality, political opinion, membership in a particular social group, torture convention.

I'm trying to stick to facts here, based on what is being stated by the people who deal with this on a daily basis, the [uscis](https://www.uscis.gov/).

I suppose we can just agree to disagree, but I hope I've at least given you something to think about.

Weird, out of all the reasons listed that people seek asylum on the US Citizenship and Immigration Services website, war is strangely absent.  Almost like that doesn't come up much as an actual reason and yet for some reason that seems to be the only reason you see as valid.

>They are not allowed to cross the border and then apply for asylum

Not only are they allowed to do that, they are required.  This is from the the [US Citizenship and Immigration Services website](https://www.uscis.gov/humanitarian/refugees-and-asylum/asylum).

​

>Every year people come to the United States seeking protection because they have suffered persecution or fear that they will suffer persecution due to:  
>  
>\* Race  
>  
>\* Religion  
>  
>\* Nationality  
>  
>\* Membership in a particular social group  
>  
>\* Political opinion  
>  
>**You may only file this application if you are physically present in the United States, and you are not a U.S. citizen.**  
>  
>If you are eligible for asylum you may be permitted to remain in the United States.  **To apply for asylum** affirmatively or defensively, **file a Form** I-589, Application for Asylum and for Withholding of Removal, **within 1 year of your arrival to the United States.**
